newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary PM says ready to testify in "Tocsik affair.
newsitem.headline: Hungary PM says ready to testify in "Tocsik affair.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn told Parliament on Monday he was ready to testify before an inquiry into a 1996 privatisation scandal known as the "Tocsik affair".
"I am ready to appear...before Parliament's committee, should it be required," the official news agency MTI quoted Horn as saying.

A special parliamentary committee was formed last December to look into the Tocsik affair, in which Marta Tocsik, an adviser to state privatisation agency APV, received 800 million forints ($4.7 million) for negotiating land deals with municipalities on APV's behalf.
The discovery of the payments led Horn to dismiss the entire APV board and the minister in charge of privatisation, Tamas Suchman, last October.

A Budapest court started proceedings in the case in January, and at the request of Chief Prosecutor Kalman Gyorgyi, Parliament last week lifted the immunity of Laszlo Boldvai, treasurer and MP of the Socialist Party, following evidence that may implicate him in the affair.
Earlier press reports said part of the success fee paid to Tocsik ended up in the accounts of organisations under the influence of people with close ties to the two ruling parties.

Horn told Parliament neither the government nor the governing Socialist Party was involved in the privatisation scandal, and noted that the authorities had recovered 600 million forints of the money paid to Tocsik.
Opposition parties have said Horn and Ivan Peto, head of the junior coalition party Free Democrats, bear ultimate political responsibility for the affair.
